script: I finally took the pill—now I am seeing her smile, and everything changes.. I was living in a flat that felt like a tomb, six months of my wife begging me to come back while I kept telling her there was no hope. And then… she started moving on with her life. We're about to file for divorce officially. I am moving out. In that mess, I hit a new low and my psychiatrist suggested a new anti‑depressant. I finally said yes. It wasn't a miracle pill, but it shifted my view. After a few weeks, joy started slipping back into my head. I remembered how stunning she looked on our wedding day—laughing mid‑vows because she was deliriously happy to be marrying me. I remembered the life we built and loved together. She'd pulled me and the kids from our quiet routine into excitement, fun, and community. Those kids became her kids, too. And after a brutal year that almost broke her… I broke. I was convinced I had to leave. I said harsh things, accused her of manipulating me, said I didn't enjoy most of our life. And for most of it, I was happier than ever, and I even told her that at the time. I didn't see how happy we had been for so long, and it got worse as time went on. I WAS happy, I just couldn't hold onto it. I was as happy as I could be. Each adventure was enough on its own. But now that I can see more, it's devastating. I was so sure we didn't have a wonderful love story. But that's exactly what it was. I told her she wanted all of it and dragged me along. I forgot my own ambition and hopes. I'd forgotten who was right in front of me—the incredible woman I'd fallen in love with dozens of times. When I finally got there, I told her. But that was another cruelty. She's been trying to let go, and now I am denying her that. I opened my eyes, with more capacity for love, joy, and beauty than ever before… and all I see is the pain I caused. I told my psychiatrist I didn't like how anti‑depressants used to make me feel. I resisted trying another because I assumed they'd all make me feel numb. I had no idea how wrong I was.
